# 1. Purpose and scope

This report does three jobs with one IMF World Economic Outlook (WEO) file.

1. **Cleans and reconciles** the raw wide file, so every later number can be traced back to a tested table.
2. **Describes world economic power** at four levels: individual countries, country groups (G7, G20, BRICS+ and others), IMF regions, and the world as a whole.
3. **Builds a classification model** that estimates the likelihood that a low-income or a high-income country moves into debt distress within two years. The model uses macroeconomic fundamentals, external buffers and fiscal space, and is judged mainly by the area under the ROC curve (AUC-ROC) and by precision-recall (average precision).

All code is flat and procedural: `data.table` for data work, `ggplot2` for graphics, `ggiraph` for hover-able interactive versions in the HTML report. Static versions of the same plots are used in DOCX and PDF output.

```{r setup}
library(data.table)

    plot.background    = element_rect(fill = "#F7F4EF", colour = NA),
    panel.background   = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", colour = NA),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#DDE3EA", linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.line.y        = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y       = element_blank(),

    axis.title         = element_text(colour = "#4A5568"),
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, colour = "#0A1628"),
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(colour = "#4A5568", size = 9.5, margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.caption       = element_text(colour = "#94A3B8", face = "italic", size = 8),
    plot.title.position   = "plot",
    plot.caption.position = "plot",

    legend.title       = element_blank(),

    legend.key         = element_rect(fill = "#F7F4EF", colour = NA),

  opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.25;"),

src <- "Source: IMF World Economic Outlook, April 2026"

data.table(
```

# 2. Data preparation and inspection

**Why.** The IMF file is wide: one row per country-indicator series and one column per year (1980-2031). Modelling, joins and plotting all need a long table with one observation per row. The series code (for example `IMF.RES:WEO(9.0.0),GBR.NGDPD.A`) hides the country code and the indicator code, so both are extracted first.

**How.** `fread()` reads the file, two `sub()` calls pull out the ISO code and the indicator code, and `melt()` turns the 52 year columns into a `year` and a `value` column. Years after each series' latest-actual year are tagged *Projection*. Fiscal-year labels such as `FY2024/25` are reduced to their first four digits.

```{r read-clean}
raw <- fread("~/imf/weo/IMF_WEO.csv", na.strings = c("", "NA", "n/a", "--"))

raw[, code := sub("^.*,", "", SERIES_CODE)]
raw[, `:=`(
  ISO = sub("\\..*", "", code),
  IND = sub("^[A-Z0-9]+\\.(.+)\\.[A-Z]$", "\\1", code),
  last_actual = suppressWarnings(as.integer(substr(gsub("[^0-9]", "", LATEST_ACTUAL_ANNUAL_DATA), 1, 4)))
)]
n_noflag <- raw[is.na(last_actual), .N]
raw[is.na(last_actual), last_actual := 2024L]
raw[, kind := fifelse(grepl("^[A-Z]{3}$", ISO), "Country", "Aggregate")]

long <- melt(
  raw,
  id.vars = c("ISO", "COUNTRY", "kind", "IND", "INDICATOR", "UNIT", "SCALE", "last_actual"),
  measure.vars = as.character(1980:2031),
  variable.name = "year", value.name = "value"
)
long[, `:=`(year = as.integer(as.character(year)), value = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(value)))]
long <- long[!is.na(value)]
long[, status := fifelse(year <= last_actual, "Actual", "Projection")]

# Raw data are written to disk before anything else is changed
fwrite(long, "IMF_WEO_clean_long.csv")

long[, .(
  observations = .N,
  countries    = uniqueN(ISO[kind == "Country"]),
  aggregates   = uniqueN(ISO[kind == "Aggregate"]),
  indicators   = uniqueN(IND),
  first_year   = min(year),
  last_year    = max(year),
  projection_share_pct = round(100 * mean(status == "Projection"), 1)
)] |> knitr::kable(caption = "Shape of the cleaned long table (saved as IMF_WEO_clean_long.csv)")
```

## 2.1 Reconciliation checks

**Why.** Before trusting any group or regional total, the file must agree with itself. Three kinds of agreement are tested: no duplicated keys, parts adding up to the whole, and IMF aggregates matching the sum of the countries inside them.

**How.** Each check sums nominal GDP (`NGDPD`, US$ billion) over the parts and compares it with the IMF's published total. The gap is `(sum of parts / published total - 1) x 100`. A gap within +/-1 per cent is treated as a pass.

First, the country groups used throughout the report (by ISO code, so names cannot cause mismatches). ASEAN-5 follows the IMF definition (Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand). A first version of this list used Viet Nam instead of Singapore, and the reconciliation below caught the 17 per cent gap that resulted, which is exactly what these checks are for.

```{r groups}
groups <- rbindlist(list(
  data.table(group = "G7",         ISO = c("USA", "JPN", "DEU", "GBR", "FRA", "ITA", "CAN")),
  data.table(group = "G20",        ISO = c("USA", "CHN", "JPN", "DEU", "GBR", "FRA", "ITA", "CAN", "IND", "BRA", "RUS", "KOR", "AUS", "MEX", "IDN", "SAU", "ARG", "ZAF", "TUR")),
  data.table(group = "BRICS+",     ISO = c("BRA", "RUS", "IND", "CHN", "ZAF", "EGY", "ETH", "IRN", "ARE", "IDN")),
  data.table(group = "ASEAN-5",    ISO = c("IDN", "MYS", "PHL", "SGP", "THA")),
  data.table(group = "EU Big-4",   ISO = c("DEU", "FRA", "ITA", "ESP")),
  data.table(group = "Gulf (GCC)", ISO = c("SAU", "ARE", "KWT", "QAT", "BHR", "OMN"))
))

groups[!ISO %in% long$ISO] |> knitr::kable(caption = "Group members missing from the data (empty = all found)")
```

```{r reconcile}
dups <- long[, .N, by = .(ISO, IND, year)][N > 1, .N]

gdp <- long[IND == "NGDPD"]
world <- gdp[COUNTRY == "World", .(year, world = value)]

rec1 <- merge(gdp[kind == "Country", .(parts = sum(value)), by = year], world, by = "year")[, check := "Sum of countries vs World"]
rec2 <- merge(gdp[COUNTRY %in% c("Advanced Economies", "Emerging Market and Developing Economies"), .(parts = sum(value)), by = year], world, by = "year")[, check := "Advanced + EMDE vs World"]
rec3 <- merge(gdp[ISO %in% groups[group == "G7", ISO], .(parts = sum(value)), by = year], gdp[COUNTRY == "G7", .(year, world = value)], by = "year")[, check := "Sum of 7 countries vs IMF G7 row"]
rec4 <- merge(gdp[ISO %in% groups[group == "ASEAN-5", ISO], .(parts = sum(value)), by = year], gdp[COUNTRY == "ASEAN-5", .(year, world = value)], by = "year")[, check := "Sum of 5 countries vs IMF ASEAN-5 row"]

rec <- rbindlist(list(rec1, rec2, rec3, rec4))
rec[, gap_pct := (parts / world - 1) * 100]

rec[year %in% c(1990, 2000, 2010, 2020, 2024), .(year, check, parts = round(parts), published = round(world), gap_pct = round(gap_pct, 2))][order(check, year)] |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Reconciliation of nominal GDP, US$ billion")

rec[, .(max_abs_gap_pct = round(max(abs(gap_pct)), 2), years_outside_1pct = sum(abs(gap_pct) > 1)), by = check] |>
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf("Summary of gaps over all years (duplicate keys found: %d; series without an actual-year flag, set to 2024: %d)", dups, n_noflag))
```

```{r reconcile-plot}
rec[, tip := paste0(check, "\n", year, ": ", round(gap_pct, 2), "%")]

p <- ggplot(rec, aes(year, gap_pct, colour = check)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#0A1628", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line_interactive(aes(tooltip = check, data_id = check), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point_interactive(aes(tooltip = tip, data_id = tip), size = 1.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(title = "Do the IMF aggregates add up?",
       subtitle = "Gap between the sum of the parts and the published total, nominal GDP (% of total)",
       x = NULL, y = "Gap (%)", caption = src)

if (html) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9, height_svg = 4.8, options = gopts) else p
```

A near-zero line means the file is internally consistent, so group and regional totals built from country rows can be compared with the IMF's own rows without adjustment.

## 2.2 Wide analysis panel

```{r wide}
ind_keep <- c("NGDPD", "PPPSH", "LP", "NGDPDPC", "NGDP_RPCH", "PCPIPCH", "GGXWDG_NGDP", "GGXCNL_NGDP", "BCA_NGDPD")

wide <- dcast(long[IND %in% ind_keep], ISO + COUNTRY + kind + year ~ IND, value.var = "value")
setorder(wide, ISO, year)

# Population (LP) is an index for IMF aggregates and is absent for "World",
# so world population is rebuilt as the sum of country populations
world_pop <- wide[kind == "Country", .(world_pop = sum(LP, na.rm = TRUE)), by = year]
world_tot <- merge(wide[COUNTRY == "World", .(year, world_gdp = NGDPD)], world_pop, by = "year")
cty <- merge(wide[kind == "Country"], world_tot, by = "year")
cty[, `:=`(
  name      = iconv(sub(",.*", "", COUNTRY), from = "UTF-8", to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT"),
  gdp_share = NGDPD / world_gdp * 100,
  pop_share = LP / world_pop * 100,
  ppp_share = PPPSH
)]

# Indicators: nominal GDP (US$ bn), PPP share of world GDP (%), population (millions),
# GDP per head (US$), real growth (%), CPI inflation (%), gross debt (% GDP),
# fiscal balance (% GDP), current account (% GDP)
cty[year == 2024, .(countries = .N, with_gdp = sum(!is.na(NGDPD)), with_growth = sum(!is.na(NGDP_RPCH)), with_debt = sum(!is.na(GGXWDG_NGDP)), with_ca = sum(!is.na(BCA_NGDPD)))] |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Country coverage of the main indicators in 2024")
```

# 3. World power

**Why.** "Power" has no single measure, so three standard weights are combined: share of world nominal GDP (market weight), share of world PPP GDP (real purchasing weight) and share of world population (scale). 

**How.** For country $i$ in year $t$, with each share expressed in per cent of the world total,

$$
P_{it} \;=\; \tfrac{1}{3}\left(s^{GDP}_{it} + s^{PPP}_{it} + s^{POP}_{it}\right),
\qquad s^{GDP}_{it} = \frac{GDP_{it}}{GDP^{World}_t}\times 100 .
$$

The index $P_{it}$ is the average of the three shares. It is easy to explain and it moves in the expected direction: large, populous, productive economies score highest. Years after each series' latest actual value are IMF projections.

```{r power-calc}
cty[, power := (gdp_share + ppp_share + pop_share) / 3]
cty[, rank := frank(-power, ties.method = "min", na.last = "keep"), by = year]

top2024 <- cty[year == 2024][order(-power)][1:10]

power_long <- melt(top2024, id.vars = c("ISO", "name"), measure.vars = c("gdp_share", "ppp_share", "pop_share"), variable.name = "measure", value.name = "share")
power_long[, measure := fcase(measure == "gdp_share", "Nominal GDP", measure == "ppp_share", "PPP GDP", measure == "pop_share", "Population")]
power_long[, name := factor(name, levels = rev(top2024$name))]
power_long[, tip := paste0(name, "\n", measure, ": ", round(share, 1), "% of world")]

p <- ggplot(power_long, aes(name, share, fill = measure, tooltip = tip, data_id = tip)) +
  geom_col_interactive(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal[c(1, 4, 3)]) +
  labs(title = "Ten largest powers in 2024: three ways to weigh them",
       subtitle = "Share of the world total (%)", x = NULL, y = "Share of world (%)", caption = src)

if (html) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9, height_svg = 5.8, options = gopts) else p
```

```{r power-trend}
top6 <- top2024[1:6, ISO]

p <- ggplot(cty[ISO %in% top6 & year >= 1990], aes(year, power, colour = name)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 2025.5, xmax = 2031.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#D4A017", alpha = 0.12) +
  annotate("text", x = 2028.5, y = Inf, label = "IMF projections", vjust = 1.6, size = 3, colour = "#8A6D0B") +
  geom_line_interactive(aes(tooltip = name, data_id = name), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point_interactive(aes(tooltip = paste0(name, " (", year, "): ", round(power, 1)), data_id = paste0(name, year)), size = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(title = "Economic weight of the six leading powers, 1990-2031",
       subtitle = "Power index = average of GDP, PPP-GDP and population shares (% of world)",
       x = NULL, y = "Power index (%)", caption = src)

if (html) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9, height_svg = 5, options = gopts) else p
```

```{r power-rank}
yrs <- c(1990, 2000, 2010, 2024, 2031)
in_top10 <- cty[year %in% yrs & rank <= 10, unique(name)]

dcast(cty[year %in% yrs & name %in% in_top10], name ~ year, value.var = "rank")[order(`2024`)] |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Rank by power index (1 = strongest). 2031 is a projection.")
```


## 3.2 How concentrated is world output?

**Why.** If a few economies hold most of world output, shocks in those economies travel everywhere. **How.** The top-5 share is the sum of the five largest GDP shares each year. The Herfindahl-Hirschman index (HHI) is $\sum_i (s_i/100)^2 \times 10{,}000$, which would be 10,000 for one dominant economy and near 0 for many equal ones.

```{r concentration}
conc <- cty[!is.na(gdp_share), .(top5 = sum(head(sort(gdp_share, decreasing = TRUE), 5)), hhi = sum((gdp_share / 100)^2) * 10000), by = year]

p <- ggplot(conc[year >= 1990], aes(year, top5, group = 1, tooltip = paste0(year, "\nTop-5 share: ", round(top5, 1), "%\nHHI: ", round(hhi)), data_id = year)) +
  geom_area(fill = "#2C7BB6", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(colour = "#1E3A5F", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point_interactive(colour = "#1E3A5F", size = 1.6) +
  labs(title = "Share of world GDP held by the five largest economies",
       subtitle = "Hover for the HHI concentration index", x = NULL, y = "Top-5 share (%)", caption = src)

if (html) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9, height_svg = 4.4, options = gopts) else p
```

# 5. Country groups

**Why.** Blocs such as the G7 and BRICS+ are how world power is usually discussed, so each group is turned into a single yearly series. **How.** Each country row is joined to the group list (a country such as India belongs to several groups). Totals are sums; growth, debt and current-account balances are **GDP-weighted means**, with each country's nominal GDP of the same year as its weight:

$$
\bar{x}_{gt} \;=\; \frac{\sum_{i\in g} w_{it}\,x_{it}}{\sum_{i\in g} w_{it}},\qquad w_{it}=GDP_{it}.
$$

Inflation uses the median, because a single hyperinflation country would distort a weighted mean.

```{r group-calc}
gp <- merge(groups, cty[!is.na(NGDPD)], by = "ISO", allow.cartesian = TRUE)

gsum <- gp[, .(
  gdp       = sum(NGDPD),
  ppp_share = sum(ppp_share, na.rm = TRUE),
  pop_share = sum(pop_share, na.rm = TRUE),
  growth    = weighted.mean(NGDP_RPCH, NGDPD, na.rm = TRUE),
  infl      = median(PCPIPCH, na.rm = TRUE),
  debt      = weighted.mean(GGXWDG_NGDP, NGDPD, na.rm = TRUE),
  ca        = weighted.mean(BCA_NGDPD, NGDPD, na.rm = TRUE)
), by = .(group, year)]
gsum <- merge(gsum, world_tot, by = "year")
gsum[, gdp_share := gdp / world_gdp * 100]

ppp_wide <- dcast(gsum[group %in% c("G7", "BRICS+")], year ~ group, value.var = "ppp_share")
cross_year <- ppp_wide[`BRICS+` > G7, min(year)]
```

```{r group-ppp}
p <- ggplot(gsum[year >= 1990], aes(year, ppp_share, colour = group)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 2025.5, xmax = 2031.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#D4A017", alpha = 0.12) +
  geom_line_interactive(aes(tooltip = group, data_id = group), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point_interactive(aes(tooltip = paste0(group, " ", year, ": ", round(ppp_share, 1), "% of world PPP GDP"), data_id = paste0(group, year)), size = 1.1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(title = "Share of world PPP GDP by country group",
       subtitle = paste0("BRICS+ overtakes the G7 in ", cross_year, "; shaded = projections; groups overlap"),
       x = NULL, y = "Share of world PPP GDP (%)", caption = src)

if (html) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9, height_svg = 5, options = gopts) else p
```

```{r group-growth}
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#64748B", linewidth = 0.3) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 2025.5, xmax = 2031.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#D4A017", alpha = 0.12) +
```

# 6. IMF regions

The IMF publishes its own regional aggregates. Six of them split the world into non-overlapping parts: advanced economies plus five groups of emerging and developing economies. The others (Euro Area, EU, G7, ASEAN-5) overlap with these and are used for comparison only.

```{r regions}

  COUNTRY = c("Advanced Economies", "Emerging and Developing Asia", "Emerging and Developing Europe", "Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC)", "Middle East and Central Asia", "Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA)", "Euro Area (EA)", "European Union (EU)", "G7", "ASEAN-5"),
  region  = c("Advanced economies", "EM Asia", "EM Europe", "Latin America", "Middle East & Central Asia", "Sub-Saharan Africa", "Euro Area", "European Union", "G7", "ASEAN-5"),
  part    = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)
)

rg <- merge(wide[kind == "Aggregate"], regions, by = "COUNTRY")
rg <- merge(rg, world_tot, by = "year")
rg[, gdp_share := NGDPD / world_gdp * 100]

  knitr::kable(caption = "Reconciliation: the six non-overlapping regions against the World total (US$ bn)")
```

# 7. Debt-distress classification model

## 7.1 What is predicted

The WEO file contains no list of debt crises or restructurings, so a transparent **proxy** is built from the public-debt ratio and the thresholds the IMF itself uses when it judges debt sustainability. These benchmarks are $\tau_{LIC}=55\%$ of GDP (medium-capacity benchmark of the IMF/World Bank framework for low-income countries) and $\tau_{HIC}=85\%$ of GDP (benchmark for advanced economies in the IMF market-access framework). For country $i$ in year $t$ with gross debt $D_{it}$:

$$
y_{it} \;=\; \mathbf{1}\!\left[\max\!\left(D_{i,t+1},\,D_{i,t+2}\right) \;\ge\; \tau_{g(i)}\right]
\quad\text{for country-years with } D_{it} < \tau_{g(i)} .
$$

In words: among countries that are **currently below** the threshold, did debt cross it within the next two years? Limiting the sample to countries not yet above the line stops the model from simply learning "high debt now means high debt later". The model must find early-warning signals in the fundamentals.

**Important limits of the label.** It is a debt-threshold breach, not a default, an arrears event or an IMF rating. It is a reasonable early-warning target, but it should not be read as a forecast of default.

**Income groups.** No income classification is in the file, so countries are classed by nominal GDP per head in 2023 against the World Bank thresholds: below US$1,135 is *low income*, above US$13,845 is *high income*. GDP per head is a proxy for GNI per head, and the classification is held fixed over time.

```{r income}
inc <- cty[year == 2023 & !is.na(NGDPDPC), .(ISO, name, gdppc23 = NGDPDPC)]
inc[, income := fcase(gdppc23 < 1135, "Low income", gdppc23 > 13845, "High income", default = "Middle income")]

inc[, .(countries = .N, median_gdp_per_head = round(median(gdppc23))), by = income][order(-median_gdp_per_head)] |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Income classes used for the model (GDP per head, 2023, US$)")
```

## 7.2 Predictors

Three blocks of predictors are used. Only series that exist for both low- and high-income countries at country level in the WEO are included. (External debt and debt-service ratios are published for aggregates only, and reserves are not in the file, so external buffers are measured by the current account and trade volumes.)

| Block | Variable | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| Macroeconomic fundamentals | `growth` | 3-year average real GDP growth (%) |
| | `infl` | CPI inflation, signed log scale: $\mathrm{sign}(\pi)\log(1+|\pi|)$ |
| External buffers | `ca` | 3-year average current-account balance (% GDP) |
| | `exp_g` | Export volume growth (%) |
| Fiscal space | `rev` | General-government revenue (% GDP) |
| | `pb` | Primary balance (% GDP) |
| | `int_rev` | Interest bill as % of revenue: $(PB-OB)/Rev\times 100$ |
| | `debt` | Gross debt (% GDP) |
| | `d_debt` | One-year change in gross debt (pp) |

The interest bill is the primary balance minus the overall balance. Every predictor uses only information up to year $t$, so no future data leak into the features.

```{r panel}
act <- dcast(long[status == "Actual" & kind == "Country" & IND %in% c("NGDPDPC", "NGDP_RPCH", "PCPIPCH", "BCA_NGDPD", "TX_RPCH", "GGR_NGDP", "GGXONLB_NGDP", "GGXCNL_NGDP", "GGXWDG_NGDP")], ISO + year ~ IND, value.var = "value")

grid_all <- CJ(ISO = unique(act$ISO), year = 1980:2031)
dt <- merge(grid_all, act, by = c("ISO", "year"), all.x = TRUE)
dt <- merge(dt, inc[, .(ISO, name, income)], by = "ISO")
dt <- dt[income %in% c("Low income", "High income")]
setorder(dt, ISO, year)

dt[, `:=`(
  growth  = frollmean(NGDP_RPCH, 3),
  infl    = sign(PCPIPCH) * log1p(abs(PCPIPCH)),
  ca      = frollmean(BCA_NGDPD, 3),
  exp_g   = TX_RPCH,
  rev     = GGR_NGDP,
  pb      = GGXONLB_NGDP,
  int_rev = (GGXONLB_NGDP - GGXCNL_NGDP) / GGR_NGDP * 100,
  debt    = GGXWDG_NGDP,
  d_debt  = GGXWDG_NGDP - shift(GGXWDG_NGDP),
  debt1   = shift(GGXWDG_NGDP, -1),
  debt2   = shift(GGXWDG_NGDP, -2),
  thr     = fifelse(income == "Low income", 55, 85)
), by = ISO]

dt[, y := as.integer(pmax(debt1, debt2) >= thr)]

# At-risk sample: below the threshold today, with every predictor observed
pan <- dt[debt < thr & complete.cases(growth, infl, ca, exp_g, rev, pb, int_rev, d_debt)]

# Winsorise at the 1st and 99th percentile within each income class, then standardise
pan[, `:=`(
  z_growth  = as.numeric(scale(pmin(pmax(growth,  quantile(growth,  0.01)), quantile(growth,  0.99)))),
  z_infl    = as.numeric(scale(pmin(pmax(infl,    quantile(infl,    0.01)), quantile(infl,    0.99)))),
  z_ca      = as.numeric(scale(pmin(pmax(ca,      quantile(ca,      0.01)), quantile(ca,      0.99)))),
  z_exp_g   = as.numeric(scale(pmin(pmax(exp_g,   quantile(exp_g,   0.01)), quantile(exp_g,   0.99)))),
  z_rev     = as.numeric(scale(pmin(pmax(rev,     quantile(rev,     0.01)), quantile(rev,     0.99)))),
  z_pb      = as.numeric(scale(pmin(pmax(pb,      quantile(pb,      0.01)), quantile(pb,      0.99)))),
  z_int_rev = as.numeric(scale(pmin(pmax(int_rev, quantile(int_rev, 0.01)), quantile(int_rev, 0.99)))),
  z_debt    = as.numeric(scale(pmin(pmax(debt,    quantile(debt,    0.01)), quantile(debt,    0.99)))),
  z_d_debt  = as.numeric(scale(pmin(pmax(d_debt,  quantile(d_debt,  0.01)), quantile(d_debt,  0.99))))
), by = income]

fit <- pan[!is.na(y)]

fit[, .(country_years = .N, countries = uniqueN(ISO), events = sum(y), event_rate_pct = round(100 * mean(y), 1), first_year = min(year), last_year = max(year)), by = income] |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model sample: country-years below the threshold with a known two-year outcome")
```

```{r events-plot}
ev <- fit[, .(events = sum(y), at_risk = .N), by = .(income, period = paste0(5 * (year %/% 5), "s"))]
ev[, `:=`(income = factor(income, levels = c("Low income", "High income")), tip = paste0(income, ", ", period, "\nEvents: ", events, " of ", at_risk, " country-years"))]

p <- ggplot(ev, aes(period, events, fill = income, tooltip = tip, data_id = tip)) +
  geom_col_interactive(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal[c(2, 1)]) +
  labs(title = "When did debt cross the threshold?", subtitle = "Count of onset events by five-year start period and income class",
       x = NULL, y = "Events", caption = src)

if (html) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9, height_svg = 4.4, options = gopts) else p
```

## 7.3 Model, validation and metrics

**Model.** A logistic regression is fitted separately for each income class, because the economics of a country with 40 per cent debt and 20 per cent revenue differs from one with 80 per cent debt and 40 per cent revenue:

$$
\Pr(y_{it}=1\mid x_{it}) \;=\; \frac{1}{1+\exp\!\left(-\beta_0-\mathbf{x}_{it}^{\top}\boldsymbol\beta\right)} .
$$

Each coefficient is reported as an **odds ratio per one standard deviation** of the predictor, $e^{\beta_k}$. Logistic regression is chosen because the samples are small (about 250 low-income country-years), where flexible machine-learning models overfit, and because every coefficient can be read and challenged.

**Validation.** Country-years from one country are strongly related, so ordinary random cross-validation would be too optimistic. Instead, countries are split into five folds within each income class. Each fold is predicted by a model that never saw that country: this is **out-of-fold** prediction for new countries. The pooled out-of-fold predictions feed all metrics.

**Metrics.**

- *AUC-ROC.* The ROC curve plots the true-positive rate against the false-positive rate as the alert threshold moves. AUC is the chance that a randomly chosen onset country-year receives a higher risk score than a randomly chosen non-onset one (0.5 = coin flip, 1 = perfect). With $R_j$ the rank of score $j$ among all $N$ out-of-fold scores, $n_1$ events and $n_0$ non-events:

$$
\mathrm{AUC} \;=\; \frac{\sum_{j:\,y_j=1} R_j \;-\; n_1(n_1+1)/2}{n_1\, n_0} .
$$

- *Precision-recall and average precision.* Debt-threshold crossings are rare, and in rare-event problems AUC can look good even when most alerts are false. Precision is the share of alerts that are real onsets, recall is the share of onsets caught. Average precision is the mean precision at each caught onset,

$$
\mathrm{AP} \;=\; \frac{1}{n_1}\sum_{j:\,y_j=1}\mathrm{Precision}@j ,
$$

and a model with no skill scores an AP equal to the event rate (the prevalence), so AP should be judged against that baseline, not against 1.

To see what each block of predictors adds, six models are compared: a naive debt-only benchmark, each block on its own, macro plus external (no fiscal), and the full model.

```{r cv}
specs <- data.table(
  model = c("1 Debt only", "2 Macro", "3 External buffers", "4 Fiscal space", "5 Macro + External", "6 Full model"),
  rhs   = c("z_debt + z_d_debt",
            "z_growth + z_infl",
            "z_ca + z_exp_g",
            "z_rev + z_pb + z_int_rev + z_debt + z_d_debt",
            "z_growth + z_infl + z_ca + z_exp_g",
            "z_growth + z_infl + z_ca + z_exp_g + z_rev + z_pb + z_int_rev + z_debt + z_d_debt")
)

set.seed(2026)
folds <- unique(fit[, .(income, ISO)])[, fold := sample(rep(1:5, length.out = .N)), by = income]
fit <- merge(fit, folds, by = c("income", "ISO"))
fit[, ci := match(ISO, unique(ISO)), by = income]

cv_grid <- merge(CJ(income = c("Low income", "High income"), model = specs$model, k = 1:5), specs, by = "model")

oof <- cv_grid[, {
  trn <- fit[income == g & fold != k]
  tst <- fit[income == g & fold == k]
  m   <- glm(as.formula(paste("y ~", rhs)), data = trn, family = binomial())
  .(ISO = tst$ISO, year = tst$year, ci = tst$ci, y = tst$y, p = predict(m, newdata = tst, type = "response"))
}, by = .(g = income, model, k, rhs)]

oof[, rk := frank(p), by = .(g, model)]
auc <- oof[, .(n = .N, events = sum(y), prevalence = mean(y), auc = (sum(rk[y == 1]) - sum(y) * (sum(y) + 1) / 2) / (sum(y) * (.N - sum(y)))), by = .(g, model)]

pr <- oof[order(g, model, -p)]
pr[, `:=`(tp = cumsum(y), n_alert = seq_len(.N)), by = .(g, model)]
pr[, `:=`(precision = tp / n_alert, recall = tp / sum(y), fpr = (n_alert - tp) / (.N - sum(y)), n_all = .N, n_pos = sum(y)), by = .(g, model)]

ap <- pr[y == 1, .(ap = mean(precision)), by = .(g, model)]
metrics <- merge(auc, ap, by = c("g", "model"))
metrics[, `:=`(ap_lift = ap / prevalence, g = factor(g, levels = c("Low income", "High income")))]
```

### Bootstrap uncertainty

With only a few dozen onset events, a single AUC number is fragile. Countries are resampled with replacement 200 times (a *cluster bootstrap*, so all years of a country move together) and the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of AUC and AP are reported.

```{r bootstrap}
set.seed(7)
nb   <- unique(fit[, .(income, ci)])[, .(nc = .N), by = income]
draw <- nb[, .(b = rep(1:200, each = nc), ci = sample(nc, 200 * nc, replace = TRUE)), by = income]

bs <- merge(oof[model %in% c("1 Debt only", "6 Full model"), .(g, model, ci, y, p)], draw, by.x = c("g", "ci"), by.y = c("income", "ci"), allow.cartesian = TRUE)
bs[, rk := frank(p), by = .(g, model, b)]
bs_auc <- bs[, .(auc = (sum(rk[y == 1]) - sum(y) * (sum(y) + 1) / 2) / (sum(y) * (.N - sum(y)))), by = .(g, model, b)]

bs <- bs[order(g, model, b, -p)]
bs[, `:=`(tp = cumsum(y), n_alert = seq_len(.N)), by = .(g, model, b)]
bs_ap <- bs[y == 1, .(ap = mean(tp / n_alert)), by = .(g, model, b)]

bs_all <- merge(bs_auc, bs_ap, by = c("g", "model", "b"))
ci_tab <- bs_all[, .(auc_lo = quantile(auc, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE), auc_hi = quantile(auc, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE), ap_lo = quantile(ap, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE), ap_hi = quantile(ap, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(g, model)]
ci_tab[, g := factor(g, levels = c("Low income", "High income"))]

res <- merge(metrics, ci_tab, by = c("g", "model"), all.x = TRUE)[order(g, model)]
res[, .(Group = g, Model = model, `Country-years` = n, Events = events, `Event rate` = round(prevalence, 3), AUC = round(auc, 3), `AUC 95% CI` = fifelse(is.na(auc_lo), "", paste0(round(auc_lo, 2), " - ", round(auc_hi, 2))), AP = round(ap, 3), `AP 95% CI` = fifelse(is.na(ap_lo), "", paste0(round(ap_lo, 2), " - ", round(ap_hi, 2))), `AP / base rate` = round(ap_lift, 1))] |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Out-of-fold performance by income class and model (confidence intervals for the benchmark and the full model)")
```

```{r metric-plot}
mp <- melt(res[, .(g, model, auc, ap, prevalence)], id.vars = c("g", "model", "prevalence"), variable.name = "metric", value.name = "value")
mp[, `:=`(metric = fifelse(metric == "auc", "AUC-ROC", "Average precision"), tip = paste0(g, "\n", model, "\n", fifelse(metric == "auc", "AUC-ROC", "Average precision"), ": ", round(value, 3)))]
mp[, model := factor(model, levels = rev(specs$model))]

base <- unique(mp[metric == "Average precision", .(g, metric, prevalence)])
base[, tip := paste0(g, "\nNo-skill AP = event rate = ", round(prevalence, 3))]

p <- ggplot(mp, aes(value, model, fill = model, tooltip = tip, data_id = tip)) +
  geom_col_interactive(width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_vline_interactive(data = base, aes(xintercept = prevalence, tooltip = tip, data_id = tip), linetype = "dashed", colour = "#C0392B") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal[c(9, 1, 5, 4, 7, 2)][c(6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1)]) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.05), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  facet_grid(g ~ metric) +
  labs(title = "What each block of predictors adds", subtitle = "Out-of-fold AUC-ROC and average precision; dashed red = no-skill AP (event rate)",
       x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = src)

if (html) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9, height_svg = 6.2, options = gopts) else p
```

## 7.4 ROC and precision-recall curves

```{r roc-curves}
full <- "6 Full model"
roc <- rbind(pr[, .(g, model, fpr, tpr = recall)], unique(pr[, .(g, model)])[, `:=`(fpr = 0, tpr = 0)])
roc <- merge(roc, metrics[, .(g, model, auc)], by = c("g", "model"))
roc[, `:=`(g = factor(g, levels = c("Low income", "High income")), lab = paste0(model, " (AUC ", round(auc, 2), ")"), is_full = model == full)]
setorder(roc, g, model, fpr, tpr)

p <- ggplot(roc, aes(fpr, tpr, colour = model, group = model)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#64748B") +
  geom_line_interactive(aes(tooltip = lab, data_id = paste(g, model), linewidth = is_full)) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c("FALSE" = 0.6, "TRUE" = 1.4), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal[c(9, 1, 5, 4, 7, 2)]) +
  facet_wrap(~g) +
  labs(title = "ROC curves (out-of-fold, new countries)", subtitle = "Higher and further left is better; dashed line = coin flip. Hover for the AUC.",
       x = "False-positive rate", y = "True-positive rate", caption = src)

if (html) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9.5, height_svg = 5, options = gopts) else p
```

```{r pr-curves}
prc <- pr[, .(g, model, recall, precision)]
prc <- merge(prc, metrics[, .(g, model, ap, prevalence)], by = c("g", "model"))
prc[, `:=`(g = factor(g, levels = c("Low income", "High income")), lab = paste0(model, " (AP ", round(ap, 2), ")"), is_full = model == full)]
basepr <- unique(prc[, .(g, prevalence)])

p <- ggplot(prc, aes(recall, precision, colour = model, group = model)) +
  geom_hline(data = basepr, aes(yintercept = prevalence), linetype = "dashed", colour = "#C0392B") +
  geom_line_interactive(aes(tooltip = lab, data_id = paste(g, model), linewidth = is_full)) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c("FALSE" = 0.6, "TRUE" = 1.4), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal[c(9, 1, 5, 4, 7, 2)]) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~g) +
  labs(title = "Precision-recall curves (out-of-fold, new countries)", subtitle = "Dashed red line = no-skill precision (the event rate). Hover a line for its AP.",
       x = "Recall (share of onsets caught)", y = "Precision", caption = src)

if (html) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9.5, height_svg = 5, options = gopts) else p
```

## 7.5 Choosing an alert threshold

**Why.** A risk score is only useful once someone decides what score triggers an alert. **How.** For the full model, the F1 score $=2PR/(P+R)$ (the balance of precision $P$ and recall $R$) is computed at every possible cut-off and the best is kept. A second, simpler rule alerts on the highest-scoring 20 per cent of country-years.

```{r threshold}
pr6 <- pr[model == full]
pr6[, f1 := 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)]

best <- pr6[, .SD[which.max(f1)], by = g]
best[, `:=`(fp = n_alert - tp, fn = n_pos - tp)][, tn := n_all - tp - fp - fn]

top20 <- pr6[n_alert == ceiling(0.2 * n_all)]

rbindlist(list(
  best[, .(Group = g, Rule = "Best F1", `Cut-off prob.` = round(p, 3), Alerts = n_alert, `True alerts` = tp, `False alerts` = fp, Missed = fn, Precision = round(precision, 2), Recall = round(recall, 2), F1 = round(f1, 2))],
  top20[, .(Group = g, Rule = "Top 20% riskiest", `Cut-off prob.` = round(p, 3), Alerts = n_alert, `True alerts` = tp, `False alerts` = n_alert - tp, Missed = n_pos - tp, Precision = round(precision, 2), Recall = round(recall, 2), F1 = round(f1, 2))]
))[order(Group, Rule)] |> knitr::kable(caption = "Confusion counts and scores at two alert rules (full model, out-of-fold)")
```

```{r calibration}
oof6 <- oof[model == full]
oof6[, quart := ceiling(4 * frank(p, ties.method = "first") / .N), by = g]
calib <- oof6[, .(n = .N, predicted = mean(p), observed = mean(y)), by = .(g, quart)]
cl <- melt(calib, id.vars = c("g", "quart", "n"), variable.name = "kind", value.name = "rate")
cl[, `:=`(g = factor(g, levels = c("Low income", "High income")), kind = fifelse(kind == "predicted", "Average predicted", "Observed event rate"), quart = factor(paste0("Q", quart)))]
cl[, tip := paste0(g, ", risk ", quart, " (n=", n, ")\n", kind, ": ", round(100 * rate, 1), "%")]

p <- ggplot(cl, aes(quart, rate, fill = kind, tooltip = tip, data_id = tip)) +
  geom_col_interactive(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal[c(5, 2)]) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  facet_wrap(~g, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Does a higher score mean more onsets?", subtitle = "Country-years ranked into risk quarters by the full model (Q1 lowest, Q4 highest)",
       x = "Risk quarter", y = "Rate", caption = src)

if (html) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9.5, height_svg = 4.6, options = gopts) else p
```

## 7.6 What drives the risk

Odds ratios from the full model fitted on all data. A value above 1 means a one-standard-deviation rise in that predictor raises the odds of crossing the threshold, a value below 1 means it lowers them. The bars are 95 per cent confidence intervals from the usual large-sample formula, which is only approximate with so few events.

```{r coefs}
coefs <- fit[, {
  m <- glm(as.formula(paste("y ~", specs[model == full, rhs])), data = .SD, family = binomial())
  s <- summary(m)$coefficients
  .(term = rownames(s), est = s[, 1], se = s[, 2], pval = s[, 4])
}, by = income]

coefs <- coefs[term != "(Intercept)"]
coefs[, `:=`(or = exp(est), lo = exp(est - 1.96 * se), hi = exp(est + 1.96 * se))]
coefs[, `:=`(
  block = fcase(term %in% c("z_growth", "z_infl"), "Macro fundamentals", term %in% c("z_ca", "z_exp_g"), "External buffers", default = "Fiscal space"),
  label = fcase(term == "z_growth", "GDP growth (3y avg)", term == "z_infl", "Inflation (log)", term == "z_ca", "Current account (3y avg)", term == "z_exp_g", "Export volume growth", term == "z_rev", "Revenue / GDP", term == "z_pb", "Primary balance", term == "z_int_rev", "Interest / revenue", term == "z_debt", "Debt / GDP", default = "Change in debt"),
  income = factor(income, levels = c("Low income", "High income"))
)]
coefs[, label := factor(label, levels = rev(unique(label)))]
coefs[, tip := paste0(income, "\n", label, "\nOdds ratio per 1 SD: ", round(or, 2), " (", round(lo, 2), " - ", round(hi, 2), ")\np = ", round(pval, 3))]

p <- ggplot(coefs, aes(or, label, colour = block, tooltip = tip, data_id = tip)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, colour = "#0A1628", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_linerange_interactive(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point_interactive(size = 2.8) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal[c(4, 2, 1)]) +
  facet_wrap(~income) +
  labs(title = "Odds ratios per one standard deviation", subtitle = "Log scale; line at 1 = no effect; bars = approximate 95% intervals",
       x = "Odds ratio (log scale)", y = NULL, caption = src)

if (html) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9.5, height_svg = 5, options = gopts) else p
```

```{r coef-table}
coefs[order(income, -or), .(Group = income, Block = block, Predictor = label, `Odds ratio` = round(or, 2), `95% low` = round(lo, 2), `95% high` = round(hi, 2), `p-value` = round(pval, 3))] |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Full-model coefficients")
```

## 7.7 Current risk ranking

The full model, fitted on all labelled data, is applied to each country's latest year (2023 or later) where debt is still below its threshold. The probability is the model's estimate that debt crosses the threshold within two years.

```{r risk}
score_rows <- pan[is.na(y) & year >= 2023][order(ISO, -year)][, .SD[1], by = ISO]

risk <- fit[, {
  m  <- glm(as.formula(paste("y ~", specs[model == full, rhs])), data = .SD, family = binomial())
  sc <- score_rows[income == g]
  .(ISO = sc$ISO, name = sc$name, year = sc$year, debt = sc$debt, thr = sc$thr, p = predict(m, newdata = sc, type = "response"))
}, by = .(g = income)]

risk[order(g, -p)][, head(.SD, 10), by = g][, .(Group = g, Country = name, Year = year, `Debt % GDP` = round(debt, 1), `Threshold` = thr, `Prob. of crossing within 2y` = round(p, 3))] |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Ten highest-risk countries in each income class")
```

```{r risk-plot}
rk <- risk[order(g, -p)][, head(.SD, 12), by = g]
rk[, `:=`(g = factor(g, levels = c("Low income", "High income")), tip = paste0(name, " (", year, ")\nDebt: ", round(debt, 1), "% GDP, threshold ", thr, "%\nProbability: ", round(100 * p, 1), "%"))]
rk[, label := factor(name, levels = rev(name))]

p <- ggplot(rk, aes(p, label, fill = g, tooltip = tip, data_id = tip)) +
  geom_col_interactive(width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(100 * p), "%")), hjust = -0.15, size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal[c(2, 1)]) +
  facet_wrap(~g, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Probability that debt crosses its threshold within two years", subtitle = "Twelve highest-scoring countries per income class, latest available year",
       x = "Probability", y = NULL, caption = src)

if (html) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9.5, height_svg = 5, options = gopts) else p
```

## 7.8 Limits of this model

- **Label.** The target is a debt-ratio crossing, not a default. Countries can default well below the thresholds, and rich countries can sit far above 85 per cent for decades without distress.
- **Small low-income sample.** Few low-income countries have long histories of public-debt data, so the low-income results rest on a few dozen events and the confidence intervals are wide. Treat low-income AUC and AP as indicative.
- **Missing buffers.** Reserves, external debt, debt-service ratios and the currency composition of debt are not available at country level in this file. Adding them is the most valuable next step.
- **Fixed income class.** Countries are classed by 2023 income and not reclassified as they grow.
- **Overlapping windows.** Consecutive years share part of their two-year outcome window, so observations are not independent; country-level folds and the cluster bootstrap reduce but do not remove this.
- **Standardisation.** Winsorising limits and standard deviations use the full sample of each class, not each training fold. This is a small leak and does not change the ranking of models.
- **Data vintage.** WEO values are revised. The latest-actual flag is taken from the file, and series without one were set to 2024.

# 8. Key findings

```{r findings-numbers}
lead <- top2024[1, name]
lead_p <- round(top2024[1, power], 1)
second <- top2024[2, name]
cn_nom <- round(usc[year == 2024, nominal])
cn_ppp <- round(usc[year == 2024, ppp])
ae90 <- round(rg[region == "Advanced economies" & year == 1990, gdp_share])
ae24 <- round(rg[region == "Advanced economies" & year == 2024, gdp_share])
asia24 <- round(rg[region == "EM Asia" & year == 2024, gdp_share])
brics24 <- round(gsum[group == "BRICS+" & year == 2024, ppp_share])
g724 <- round(gsum[group == "G7" & year == 2024, ppp_share])
max_gap <- round(rec[, max(abs(gap_pct))], 2)

full_lic <- res[g == "Low income" & model == full]
full_hic <- res[g == "High income" & model == full]
debt_lic <- res[g == "Low income" & model == "1 Debt only"]
debt_hic <- res[g == "High income" & model == "1 Debt only"]
blk_lic <- res[g == "Low income"]
blk_hic <- res[g == "High income"]
best_ap <- res[, .SD[which.max(ap)], by = g]
top_lic <- risk[g == "Low income"][order(-p)][1, name]
top_hic <- risk[g == "High income"][order(-p)][1, name]
```

**World power**

- By the three-share power index, **`r lead`** leads in 2024 (index `r lead_p`), followed by **`r second`**.
- China's nominal GDP is **`r cn_nom`%** of the United States' in 2024; in PPP terms its share of world output is **`r cn_ppp`%** of the US share.
- Advanced economies produced about **`r ae90`%** of world nominal GDP in 1990 and **`r ae24`%** in 2024, while emerging Asia rose to **`r asia24`%**.
- BRICS+ passed the G7 in PPP share of world GDP in **`r cross_year`**; in 2024 the shares are **`r brics24`%** and **`r g724`%**.

**Data quality**

- The cleaned file reconciles with the IMF's own aggregates: the largest gap in any check is **`r max_gap`%** of the published total.

**Debt-distress model**

- *Low income* (`r full_lic$events` onsets in `r full_lic$n` country-years, event rate `r round(full_lic$prevalence, 2)`): the full model has AUC **`r round(full_lic$auc, 2)`** and average precision **`r round(full_lic$ap, 2)`**. It `r ifelse(full_lic$auc > debt_lic$auc, "improves on", "does not improve on")` the debt-only benchmark (AUC `r round(debt_lic$auc, 2)`, AP `r round(debt_lic$ap, 2)`). With this few events, extra predictors can add noise as well as signal.
- *High income* (`r full_hic$events` onsets in `r full_hic$n` country-years, event rate `r round(full_hic$prevalence, 3)`): the full model has AUC **`r round(full_hic$auc, 2)`** and average precision **`r round(full_hic$ap, 2)`**, which `r ifelse(full_hic$ap > debt_hic$ap, "beats", "does not beat")` the debt-only benchmark on average precision (`r round(debt_hic$ap, 2)`; AUC `r round(debt_hic$auc, 2)`).
- *Which block carries the signal.* On their own, the fiscal-space block reaches AUC `r round(blk_lic[model == "4 Fiscal space", auc], 2)` (low income) and `r round(blk_hic[model == "4 Fiscal space", auc], 2)` (high income). Macro fundamentals alone reach `r round(blk_lic[model == "2 Macro", auc], 2)` and `r round(blk_hic[model == "2 Macro", auc], 2)`, and external buffers alone `r round(blk_lic[model == "3 External buffers", auc], 2)` and `r round(blk_hic[model == "3 External buffers", auc], 2)` (0.5 is a coin flip). Debt-threshold crossings are mainly a fiscal story in this data.
- *Best model by average precision:* `r best_ap[g == "Low income", model]` for low income and `r best_ap[g == "High income", model]` for high income.
- The highest current risk scores belong to **`r top_lic`** (low income) and **`r top_hic`** (high income).
- Read the debt-only benchmark as "distance to the threshold". A model that beats it is finding information beyond the debt level; one that does not is mostly restating it. Treat all scores as early-warning signals for a debt-threshold breach, not as forecasts of default (section 7.8).
